carousel.short: When information is free, where does the edge go?
carousel.long: When information is free, where does the edge go? Halfway through a strategy meeting, I admitted the pace of AI was overwhelming me.

Information isn't the currency anymore. When a system can research, compare and propose new directions by itself, the cost of creating new knowledge drops so low that it's not what matters. Then a clearer thought arrived.

carousel.short: Stay at the frontier, keep your core elsewhere.
carousel.long: Stay at the frontier, keep your core elsewhere. AI multiplies what a small team can do, so be at the frontier. But keep the core of your work where technology has no capabilities: people, materials, buildings, streets.

carousel.short: Diagram: The edge moves to where technology can't reach.
carousel.long: Diagram: The edge moves to where technology can't reach. Be at the frontier of the tools, and keep the core of your work in the physical world.

carousel.short: What stays scarce: judgement and trust.
carousel.long: What stays scarce: judgement and trust. Judgement about which real problems to point the machines at, and values. In Portuguese property, deals still close on trust, face to face. How many apartments before a building? Maybe hundreds.

carousel.short: Use AI to prepare the decision, and keep the decision where the building is.
carousel.long: Use AI to prepare the decision, and keep the decision where the building is. Tell me where the edge sits in your field, especially if you see it differently.

quote.short: Quote card: "Information isn't the currency anymore."
quote.long: Quote card: "Information isn't the currency anymore." Asaf Eyzenkot, Suf Zen, founder of Realization.

cover.long: AI can't pour concrete. Asaf Eyzenkot, Suf Zen, founder of Realization.
